quotes.text: As a young singer Brown was influenced by older contemporaries such as Delroy Wilson (whom he later cited as the single greatest influence on his style of singing), Errol Dunkley, John Holt, Ken Boothe, and Bob Andy.
Brown was advised by fellow Studio One artist Ellis to learn guitar to help with his songwriting, and after convincing Dodd to buy him an instrument, was taught the basics by Ellis.
Bob Marley cited Brown as his favourite singer, dubbing him "The Crown Prince of Reggae", and Brown would prove influential on future generations of reggae singers.
With over 25 years experience on the reggae scene, Dennis Brown helped lay the foundation for today's reggae/dancehall stars.
Love & Hate, featuring 15 universal meditations, transcends the typical greatest-hits genre.
Brown's silken voice, relaxed delivery, and righteous lyricism won him a level of esteem among Jamaicans second only to that afforded Bob Marley himself.
Sensitive production from Gibbs and Errol Thompson, and tough, unfailingly solid instrumental work from Gibbs' studio band The Professionals only add to the greatness of this landmark release.
Brown manages to sustain throughout the entirety of this 10-track release a powerful note opened by the bracing roots cut "Deliverance Will Come".
